outcome.technical: MONOTONE UNION, implemented. (a) guard-history-rewrite.py: git_calls(command, depth, joined=False) - joined=True skips parts_read_alone at every depth, i.e. the reading main had of the raw joined view, kept as a reading rather than deleted. New command_reading(command) -> (calls, strict): when every part reads alone, the joined parse alone, strict False; otherwise the joined view's parse (None-safe) merged with git_calls of every part that ends closed and tokenizes alone, strict True. _merged() is a multiset union so one operation found by two readings is named once. always_refused, amend_requested, stash_operations and reset_targets grade the merged calls, and when strict add their text patterns (union, never either-or); new _reset_target_text and _always_refused_calls factor the pieces. decide: early allow only for calls == [] and not strict; the xargs-git STDIN_VERB check reads the merged calls; the unparsed git -C deny keys on strict; call_trees gets the merged calls plus a session entry for the text reading's answer, appended after so reset indexes still hold. (b) _config.runnable_clauses returns per-part clauses then the joined view's clauses not already present (union); runnable_text docstring rewritten to state the union. That covers guard-release _publishers and _shell_moves and the history guard's _shell_moves. (c) guard-uncommitted reading(): new _parsed_calls uses the parser's command_reading (falls back to git_invocations); on a strict line the text shapes over the lifted view are asked first (widest loss set), then the merged calls' judgement, so neither reading can allow what the other refuses. (d) guard-secrets-read.py: no code change; it reads runnable_text, the joined view, i.e. main's reading over the shared split, and never had a per-part reading. House-template lifting happens inside split_heredocs, before every reading. MATRIX (reviewer probe run.py/cmp.py over cases.json, main export vs this tree): before the change 140 weaker rows (hist 98, sec 6, unc 20, rel 16); after it 96 (hist 54, sec 6, unc 20, rel 16), stronger hist 112. Of the 96: 92 are house-form rows - p153.allow1/allow2/allow3 (commit -m, audit-task --description, gh pr --body, each with every verb), allow4 (backquoted house form, secrets), b11 and b12 (a house-form commit/tag message that a LATER clause runs through bash -c "$(git log ...)" or git tag -l | sh: the body is lifted because it matches the template exactly; the guards cannot follow text through git's object store - flagged for a decision, not changed). The other 4 are p153.b2 and p153.b2b with <HARD-RESET> onto HEAD~1 (hist): the marker line `cat <<E'X' )"` / `cat <<E-X )"` is not the house form; main denied because its old delimiter regex read the marker as `E`, classed the rest as a shell body and so called the cwd unreadable; this tree reads the delimiter as the shell does, sees the reset run, and the ancestry check finds nothing orphaned (HEAD~1 holds the recorded commit). With a target that orphans the recorded commit (HEAD~2) both shapes deny: gu44, gu45. NOT IN THE REVIEWER'S PROBE, measured separately (11 extra shapes x 7 verbs, same driver): 22 more rows weaker than main, none house-form, from split_heredocs narrowings earlier tasks of this phase made deliberately: a body written to a file named *.sh (with or without a later `sh probe.sh`; hist 10, sec 2, unc 2, rel 2 - this is gh35's pinned allow, from the program-word rule) and a body piped to `python3 "x.py"` with the script path quoted (hist 5, unc 1 - the unquoted spelling was already data on main). The union cannot see these because every reading shares the current split. Making them deny means reverting the program-word rule and the quoted-script reading, which turns gh35 red and contradicts the history guard's module docstring - a reversal of a pinned decision, left for the orchestrator.
